item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Israel rejects Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza, says Netanyahu
item.description:
Israel rejects Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza, says Netanyahu

Submitted by MEE staff on Sun, 08/09/2026 - 13:10
PM says Israeli forces will not withdraw until Hamas 'is genuinely disarmed' and will continue to 'thwart threats'
A beekeeper tends to beehives with his sons on the roof of a destroyed building in Gaza City’s Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood on 5 August 2026 (Omar al-Qattaa/AFP)
Off

Israel has rejected US President Donald Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza and will not withdraw until Hamas fully disarms, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday.

The Board of Peace, spearheaded by Trump, announced last month that it had made a breakthrough in a plan to end the war.

Israel and Hamas agreed to the plan last year, beginning with a ceasefire. Israel has continued to carry out near-daily strikes on Gaza since agreeing to the ceasefire last October.

Trump said that Hamas had agreed to lay down its weapons.

“Israel rejects the 15-point document,” Netanyahu said at a cabinet meeting on Sunday.

The Israeli army “will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and our citizens”, he added.

Middle East Eye obtained a copy of the 15-point agreement last month. 

Under the deal, Hamas and other Palestinian factions would not hand Gaza’s weapons to Israel. Instead, the weapons would be placed under the control of a body called the National Committee.

The document seen by MEE states that the weapons would remain in Palestinian hands.

Full text: 15-point draft peace plan between Hamas and Israel in Gaza
Read More »

"No weapons will be transferred or surrendered to Israel or any non-Palestinian parties," the text states, and by the end of the disarmament process, "the National Committee alone shall retain, store, or control weapons in Gaza". 

The agreement describes weapons collection as a domestic process: "The National Committee, as the transitional authority in Gaza, shall be the sole authority for registering weapons, issuing and revoking licenses, and enforcing the law... all factions, clans, and elements of Palestinian society in Gaza shall cooperate with the National Committee in this process."

Hamas has publicly said it will not implement any part of the roadmap unless Israel meets its obligations, including a full, phased withdrawal from the territory it still controls in Gaza.

The document makes that condition central to every stage, stating that “the transition from one phase to the next will be contingent upon the verified completion of the previous phase’s obligations”, with an international commission responsible for verification.

“This is a monumental step toward lasting PEACE and SECURITY,” Trump wrote on Truth Social after the plan was revealed.

He said Israeli forces would withdraw “as disarmament is completed”, while the UN-mandated International Stabilization Force would work alongside a new Palestinian police force.

Hamas official Ghazi Hamad told Reuters at the time that the group would retain its weapons until Israel halted its attacks, allowed more aid and goods into Gaza, and withdrew its forces in accordance with the ceasefire agreement reached in October last year.

item.description:
Houthi attacks kill 11 in Yemen and target Saudi refinery

Strikes by Yemen's Houthis on Sunday killed at least 11 people, a medical source in the Yemeni port city of Mokha has told AFP, after an earlier drone salvo targeted a Saudi oil refinery on the Red Sea coast.

A years-long truce in Yemen's civil war between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed internationally recognised government appeared to collapse last month.

It came as the Houthis announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, hitting Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and the kingdom's oil infrastructure, in parallel with Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

A medical source in Mokha, held by Yemen's internationally recognised, Aden-based government, said three civilians and eight military personnel had been killed in the Houthi attacks. 

A further 32 individuals were wounded, six of them civilians, the source added, explaining all the civilian casualties had been a result of strikes on Mokha's port.

The Houthis' military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had targeted "Saudi enemy" troops and equipment in the area with missiles and drones.

Earlier, Saree said the Houthis had struck an oil facility on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast after the Gulf kingdom's energy ministry said it had extinguished a fire at the Jazan site.

He added that the attack on the facility operated by Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil firm Aramco was launched in response to incursions by drones from the Gulf monarchy into northwest Yemen.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] India to Israel and back: How a fake IRGC quote on nuclear weapons reached Netanyahu’s speech
item.description:
India to Israel and back: How a fake IRGC quote on nuclear weapons reached Netanyahu’s speech

Submitted by Nadav Rapaport on Sun, 08/09/2026 - 13:48
Report finds the alleged quote about nuclear weapons first appeared on an Indian pro-Israel account on X before being amplified by Israeli and US figures
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrives for a meeting with US President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington on 28 July 2026 (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images/AFP)
Off

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu repeated an alleged quote attributed to a senior Iranian commander about Tehran's determination to develop nuclear weapons, even though the statement had no identified primary source and was later traced to an Indian pro-Israel account on X.

An investigation by Israeli news outlet Ynet and New York Times journalist Ronen Bergman found that Netanyahu used the alleged quote, attributed to Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) chief Ahmad Vahidi, in an official address to warn Israelis about Iran's nuclear plans.

Ynet's investigation traced the source of Netanyahu's remarks to Ritika, an Indian Hindu-nationalist and pro-Israel X account, which posted the alleged quote on 5 August.

"There will be no discussion over enriched uranium or nuclear weapons. As long as the United States and Israel possess nuclear weapons, we will continue working on them for our national security. If they disarm, we will disarm," the post attributed to Vahidi said.

According to Ynet, the quote began circulating rapidly after it was posted.

About four and a half hours later, Mossad Commentary, which presents itself as an unofficial account of Israel's intelligence agency on X but has no connection to the Mossad foreign intelligence agency, repeated the claim to its more than 1 million followers.

"THERE WILL BE NO FINAL DEAL. The sooner we understand that, the better," the account said, before citing the alleged remarks by Vahidi.

The account added: "The regime is not preparing to abandon its nuclear ambitions. It is buying time. There will be no deal." 

Activists raise alarm over 'flood' of military supplies from India to Israel
Read More »

Israel’s Channel 14 repeated the alleged Vahidi quote, describing it as the first direct admission by an Iranian official that Tehran was developing a nuclear bomb. It did not provide a primary source for the quotation.

Channel 14 News is widely regarded in Israel as a mouthpiece for Netanyahu and his far-right government.

A recent report found that the Israeli government had bought millions of shekels worth of commercial airtime from the channel in recent years.

Ynet reported that Yair Netanyahu, the prime minister's eldest son, subsequently reposted content from the two Israeli accounts to his near-300,000 followers on X.

Yair Netanyahu is one of the most influential figures in the Prime Minister's inner circle, with numerous reports indicating that he and his mother, Sara Netanyahu, are heavily involved in the prime minister’s decision-making.

Netanyahu's eldest son is known for promoting far-right politics and false information through his social media accounts, with many of Netanyahu's Likud party members seeking his approval.

A record of false claims

About two hours later, Netanyahu himself referred to the alleged statement during an official ceremony in Jerusalem.

"Today, we heard the commander of the Revolutionary Guards, Vahidi, explicitly declare Iran’s intention to continue developing nuclear weapons - ‘continue’, as he put it," Netanyahu said, according to Ynet's investigation.

Narendra Modi: India’s most pro-Israel leader
Read More »

The alleged quote subsequently spread to the United States. 

According to Ynet, Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the United Nations, reposted the Channel 14 report before later deleting it. US conservative commentator Mark Levin also reposted it.

Fox News later reported that Vahidi had said Iran would continue working on nuclear weapons as long as the US and Israel possessed them. The outlet subsequently clarified its report, saying the remarks "were previously taken out of context and amplified as comments made this week".

The alleged quote continued to circulate in Israeli media, with journalists close to Netanyahu, including Yaakov Bardugo and Avishay Ben Haim, repeating the prime minister’s warning on Israeli television, Ynet reported.

The Israeli foreign ministry's Persian-language X account also posted Netanyahu's remarks about Vahidi.

About 13 hours after the original post appeared on the Indian X account, Fox News reported on the alleged statement, saying it was "intensifying concerns that Iran is using negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz to postpone concessions on its nuclear program".

Two days later, the outlet clarified that Vahidi's remarks "were previously taken out of context and amplified as comments made this week".

Two hours after Fox's initial report, Asian News International, a major Indian news outlet, repeated the claim, citing Israeli media reports.

Israel's disinformation campaign

Vahidi's alleged quote, Ynet said, served Netanyahu to bolster his claim that Iran seeks to develop a nuclear weapon amid reports suggesting that Netanyahu opposes a deal between the US and Iran.

In June, Netanyahu told Channel 14 News that "as long as I am prime minister, Iran will not have nuclear weapons", adding that he saved Israel from "annihilation" twice by claiming Iran possessed atomic bombs.

How Israel uses Bollywood to whitewash the occupation 
Read More »

While Ynet could not determine whether Netanyahu or his inner circle directed the circulation of Vahidi's alleged quote, the investigation pointed "to a series of familiar markers of disinformation distribution".

It said that Netanyahu had faced similar accusations in the past.

In September 2024, Netanyahu’s office allegedly provided the UK-based Jewish Chronicle and Germany-based Bild newspaper with false information claiming that Hamas intended to smuggle Israeli captives through the Rafah area between the Gaza Strip and Egypt to Iran.

Two Netanyahu aides are also under investigation over allegations that classified documents were leaked to influence Israeli public opinion about military operations in Rafah.

Ynet's investigation said recent reports suggested Israeli influence operations had increasingly targeted audiences outside Israel, including in the US, amid growing criticism of Israel's actions in Gaza and Iran from both Democratic and Republican figures.

Last month, Iran's embassy in India also accused Indian media of spreading false information about Iran.

"Indian media should not compromise the public trust and its professional credibility by disseminating fake and fabricated news," the embassy said, adding that it expected outlets to "avoid participating in external propaganda efforts".

item.description:
Trump could declare victory if Iran reopens Strait of Hormuz: Report

US President Donald Trump is prepared to declare victory in the war with Iran if Tehran restores shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, according to The Wall Street Journal.

US officials told the newspaper that Trump has privately indicated he could abandon efforts to secure a nuclear agreement with Iran in return for reopening the strategic waterway.

Trump is reportedly willing to let negotiations continue, particularly while petrol prices in the US remain stable.

A White House official said Washington had achieved its military objectives in Iran and that Trump was now prioritising the movement of oil through the strait. The US would maintain forces in the region and could attack Iran again if Tehran targeted vessels, the report added.

Trump also believes Iran cannot rebuild its nuclear facilities during his presidency after US forces struck three sites during the June 2025 war. He expects US intelligence to detect any reconstruction work and believes the threat of further attacks will deter Tehran, according to the newspaper.

Officials said Trump could extend the ceasefire indefinitely and end the US naval blockade if shipping resumes and Washington retains the ability to prevent Iran from restoring its nuclear programme.

item.description:
Egypt calls for full Israeli withdrawal and unrestricted aid access to Gaza

Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty has called for Israel to withdraw completely from Gaza and allow the sustained delivery of humanitarian aid under US President Donald Trump’s peace plan.

Abdelatty made the demand during a telephone conversation with Nikolay Mladenov, director-general of Trump’s Board of Peace, Egypt’s Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

The two officials reviewed efforts to implement the plan and discussed the proposed deployment of the International Stabilization Force, which is expected to assume responsibility for security inside the Palestinian territory.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Israeli general says Gaza should remain ‘destroyed for generations’
item.description:
Israeli general says Gaza should remain ‘destroyed for generations’

Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Sun, 08/09/2026 - 21:14
Giora Eiland says Palestinian despair serves Israel and demands permanent control beyond the Yellow Line
Palestinian residential salvage what they can from an apartment targeted in overnight Israeli airstrikes in Gaza City on August 2, 2026. (Omar Al Qattaa/AFP)
Off

A former head of Israel’s National Security Council has called for Gaza to remain devastated for decades, openly presenting Palestinian despair and destruction as desirable outcomes after Israel’s genocide in the enclave.

Retired Major General Giora Eiland told Israel’s 103FM radio station on Sunday that rebuilding Gaza would run against Israeli interests.

“Israel has no interest in Gaza being rebuilt, it is better for us that it be destroyed for generations to come,” Eiland said.

“The greater the despair in Gaza and the greater the destruction, and the greater the monument to what they did on October 7, years to come, that is good" he added.

Eiland, a secular Israeli nationalist aligned with opposition politician Avigdor Lieberman, opposes Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu politically.

Yet his prescriptions for Gaza have frequently gone beyond Netanyahu’s publicly declared policies.

Calls for Israel to occupy Gaza land

Eiland described the 15-point Gaza plan backed by US President Donald Trump as “pro-Hamas”. Netanyahu formally rejected the proposal on Sunday.

“In war...the losing side loses. Germany, which lost the Second World War, was forced to surrender 25 percent of its territory,” he noted.

Eiland used the comparison to argue that Israel should retain the Yellow Line, which marks the territory its military occupies inside Gaza which Israel has continued to expand and may ultimately amount to 70 percent of Gaza's territory.

“Along with this, there is the territorial need for the Yellow Line, which we must not give up under any circumstances. This is a war, the enemy has lost, and we need land, not for settlement, but as a security buffer between the settlements and where the IDF can be located."

Eiland nevertheless criticised Netanyahu’s handling of Washington, arguing that Israel had become too dependent on his relationship with Trump.

Israel rejects Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza, says Netanyahu
Read More »

“I believe Israel’s entire approach towards the US in recent years has been outrageous. It relies excessively on the personal relationship between Netanyahu and Trump, which is good on some days and less so on others.”

He advised Netanyahu to accept the US plan conditionally while protecting Israel’s central demands.

"Where did Netanyahu go wrong in my opinion? You should never say no, you should always say yes but... or yes in the sense of I agree if certain points happen," he clarified.

Eiland said Israel could temporarily suspend "assassinations" in Gaza as a tactical concession to Washington but insisted it must maintain control of the Yellow Line.

Since the ceasefire took effect on 11 October, Israeli forces have killed at least 1,258 Palestinians and injured 4,139 others, the sources said.

Earlier this week the United Nations Children's Fund said that at least 300 children have been killed in the Gaza Strip by Israel over the last 10 months. 

Israel’s genocide on Gaza has killed at least 73,386 Palestinians and wounded 174,250 since 7 October 2023.
